item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports learning recommendation-aware textual representations, but the retrieved papers do not establish a lightweight, from-scratch text encoder jointly trained with NextItNet. [Recformer (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13731) represents items as attribute-text sentences and combines language understanding with recommendation objectives. [JEPA4Rec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.10512) uses masked item-text representation prediction and two-stage training. These offer representation-learning ideas, rather than verified implementations satisfying this task’s constraints. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) incorporates titles, descriptions and reviews through pretrained BERT and a self-attention backbone; its reported gains cannot establish effectiveness with only permitted text and no pretrained weights.\n\nA plausible experimental adaptation is a randomly initialized token embedding table with masked mean pooling plus an MLP, or a small word-level CNN over titles/descriptions. Combine its output with item-ID embeddings through a jointly learned projection or gate, then retain NextItNet’s residual dilated causal convolutions and one scoring head. The [original NextItNet paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163) supports the convolutional backbone; this text extension is an inference, not a verified result from the retrieved literature. Mean pooling shares lexical features cheaply; a text CNN could additionally learn short compositional phrases. Train all components together using next-item supervision, use the same item representation construction for histories and candidates, and measure whether text improves validation HR@10 under the fixed protocol."}
